key_insight: Boron redistributes toward defects in TiAl, pinning dislocations and suppressing deformation twinning to strengthen the alloy at high temperature.
engineering_relevance: Controlling boron content and defect populations could improve high-temperature TiAl strength, while accounting for brittle borides and interface-dependent adhesion.
method: Developed a high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential.
Combined grand-canonical Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulations.
Analyzed boron segregation, defect interactions, and deformation mechanisms.
evidence_signal: Polycrystalline TiAl simulations showed 9.4% higher average flow stress at 1 at.% B and 900 K, accompanied by reduced shear strain accumulation.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation-based strengthening; experimental validation and transferability beyond the studied conditions remain to be established.
paper_title: Atomistic insight into defect-mediated boron redistribution and high-temperature strengthening in TiAl alloys
